takeaway: Osteosarcoma: a teenager with night pain, bone destruction in the metaphysis and periosteal elevation; it peaks at 10 to 20 years.

question.text: A 14-year-old boy has constant left knee pain for a month that keeps him awake at night. X-ray: metaphyseal bone destruction, new bone formation and periosteal elevation. Diagnosis?
question.say: A fourteen-year-old boy has constant left knee pain, worse over a month, that keeps him awake at night. The X-ray shows bone destruction in the metaphysis of the femur, with new bone formation and periosteal elevation. What is the diagnosis?

lines.text: A 14-year-old footballer with constant knee pain that keeps him awake at night.
lines.say: This fourteen-year-old footballer has constant left knee pain, getting worse over a month, and it keeps him awake at night.

lines.text: The skin over his knee is warm and shiny.
lines.say: The skin over his knee is warm and shiny.

lines.text: On the X-ray a monster chews the metaphysis of the femur.
lines.say: (laugh) On the X-ray, a monster is chewing the metaphysis of the femur: bone destruction.

lines.text: New bone forms in a sunburst, with periosteal elevation.
lines.say: There is new bone formation in a sunburst pattern, with periosteal elevation.

lines.text: This highly malignant tumour peaks between 10 and 20 years.
lines.say: This highly malignant tumour appears between ten and twenty years of age, and again after fifty, secondary to Paget's disease.

lines.text: Remember: a teenager with metaphysis destruction and periosteal elevation has osteosarcoma.
lines.say: Remember: a teenager with metaphysis destruction and periosteal elevation has an osteosarcoma.
